transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I just don’t care about anything anymore. Like, I used to have art classes, and board-game nights with people, and I kept saying I’d get back to hiking or maybe the soccer team, but now I just… don’t. I sit in my room and everything kind of slips away.

It’s weird because I still have all my art stuff, like the paints are right there, and I think about how I should use them, and then I remember this one teacher who said color was supposed to feel alive, but it all just feels like cardboard now. So… yeah. That’s why I’m here, I think.
Do you find that things you used to enjoy, like art or spending time with friends, don’t bring you any pleasure anymore?

Yeah… yes. It’s like the pleasure part just got unplugged. Art used to be the thing I’d go to, and now I look at my paints and it’s just… stuff on a shelf. Board-game nights too—I used to like the little pieces and the joking around, and now I can’t make myself care.

I keep thinking, oh, maybe I’ll hike again, or maybe I’ll get back to soccer, but then I just sit in my room and time sort of… disappears. Like everything keeps moving without me.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Most days, yeah. I wake up and there’s this… heavy, hollow feeling in my chest, like before I even open my eyes I already know the day is going to be too much. Or not even too much—just empty.

It’s like there’s no future past the apartment walls, if that makes sense. I keep looking at the same window, the same corners of the room, and I think about how apartments all have that one weird patch of paint from where somebody tried to fix something badly… sorry, that’s not really what you asked. But yes. Most of the day, nearly every day, I feel down.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um… I think it got really constant around the following summer. Before that it was kind of coming and going, or I could pretend it was just a bad stretch, but then that summer it sort of settled in and didn’t leave.

So… about a year and four months now, I guess. It’s strange measuring it like that, because seasons make it sound like something should change, like summer to fall, fall to winter, but it all just felt the same.
Do you find that you feel tired or that you have no energy most days, even if you haven't done much?

Yeah. I mean… yes, most days I feel wiped out even when I haven’t really done anything. I can be in bed half the day, and then just taking a shower feels like this huge project. Or answering one message—just one—and it feels like I already worked a full shift.

It’s weird because I’ll lie there thinking about all the things I should do, like dishes or laundry, and then I start noticing the laundry basket has that cracked handle, and I remember I meant to buy a new one months ago… but then I’m still just lying there. So, yes. No energy, even after resting.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you can't sit still and feel restless?

Yeah… both, weirdly. Some days I can’t sit still at all. I just pace from the kitchen to the window and back again, over and over, like I’m checking for something, but I don’t even know what. Then my legs start hurting and I realize I’ve been doing it for ages.

And then other times it’s the opposite. I move so slow it’s almost embarrassing. Making coffee feels like… like lifting wet cement, like every step has this drag to it. I’ll stand there holding the mug and forget what part comes next for a second, or not forget exactly, just… everything feels too heavy and slow.
Have you had any thoughts about ending your life or that life isn’t worth living?

Yeah… I have. Not like I have some neat sentence for it, but I keep having these thoughts like… I don’t want to wake up anymore. Like if I could just not have to start another day, that would be better.

And, um… when my friend found me, I guess I was saying it out loud. I don’t even remember every word exactly, but I kept saying I couldn’t keep living like this. It’s embarrassing because her shoes were still by the door from the last time she came over, and I remember staring at them instead of looking at her… but yeah. I was saying that.
Have you noticed that you’ve completely lost interest in all activities, including things that you used to find enjoyable or important?

Yeah… that’s kind of why I’m here, honestly. I don’t care about anything anymore. Like, not just “I’m bored” care, but… I used to have art classes, and I loved those. I had this whole thing with charcoal, and I bought this stupidly expensive sketchbook because the paper felt nice, and now it’s just sitting there.

And board-game nights too—I used to be the one reminding everyone, and now if someone texts, I just… don’t go. Hiking, same thing. I used to think getting back with the soccer team mattered, like I had to get myself together for that, but now it just feels like something from somebody else’s life.

Mostly I just sit in my room and everything keeps slipping away, and I can see it happening, but I don’t feel anything strong enough to grab onto it.
